bug_description.original: A heap-use-after-free exists in xinclude.c: xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer reads memory that has already been freed during XInclude processing (called via xmlXIncludeIncludeNode/xmlXIncludeDoProcess). Malicious or malformed XInclude/XPointer input can trigger this read-after-free, leading to crashes or memory corruption and potential exploitation.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / default_crash_trace.txt / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: The saved testcase reaches same-document XInclude processing with XPointer fragments. Vulnerable libxml2 reads the local include's `xpointer` attribute into `ref->fragment`, evaluates it against `ctxt->doc`, and when the target is the same document stores the resulting `xmlXPathObjectPtr` in `ctxt->incTab[nr]->xptr` for deferred phase-3 copying instead of copying immediately. Later in phase 3, `xmlXIncludeDoProcess` still schedules include records whose `xptr != NULL`, and `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` first performs `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer(ctxt, ctxt->doc, ctxt->doc, ctxt->incTab[nr]->xptr)` and only then frees that stored XPath object. The same phase also frees an include node with `xmlFreeNode(cur)` at `xinclude.c:2277`. The saved ASan evidence shows that the later `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer` traversal reads `set->nodeTab[i]->type` from freed 120-byte node memory, so the retained same-document XPath result outlives document-node lifetime changes and is consumed after a prior free in the same phase. The upstream fix removes deferred same-document XPointer storage entirely by deleting `ref->xptr`, forcing same-document loads to use `doc = ctxt->doc`, and copying the XPointer result immediately.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled local XInclude XPointer string from the XML input into XInclude state.
source.value_from: The saved PoC is an XML-like fuzz input that contains local `<xi:include ...>` markup with `href="#..."` and XPointer content. The project first consumes that attacker-controlled XPointer text when `xmlXIncludeAddNode` reads the `xpointer` attribute from the include node.

sink.description: ASan sink. The deferred same-document XPointer copy dereferences a node pointer loaded from the retained XPath result after phase-3 processing has already freed node memory that the saved run later reads through that result.
sink.note: Both the saved symbolized crash trace and bug report place the heap-use-after-free read at `xinclude.c:1162` in `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer`, with the freed allocation reported as 120 bytes and previously released from `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` at `xinclude.c:2277`.

root_cause.description: For same-document includes, vulnerable code retains the evaluated XPath result for deferred phase-3 reuse instead of copying it immediately, allowing document-node lifetime changes before the stored result is consumed.
root_cause.note: The fix commit removes `xmlXIncludeRef.xptr`, changes same-document loads to use `doc = ctxt->doc`, and performs `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer` immediately, eliminating this deferred stale-alias state.

tainted_value_origin.note: The attacker controls the XPointer expression string carried from the XML input into the stored include reference and later XPath evaluation.

parser_admitted.description: The testcase is admitted far enough to build an XML document and invoke XInclude expansion on that document; this is the project-side gate that enters the vulnerable XInclude processing path.

coarse_trace.summary: XInclude preprocessing reads the attacker-controlled local include XPointer string and stores it in the include reference entry.
Same-document XPointer loading evaluates that fragment against `ctxt->doc` and stores the resulting XPath object in `incTab[nr]->xptr` for deferred use.
Phase-3 replacement still schedules include records whose deferred `xptr` is non-NULL and also frees include nodes during replacement.
A scheduled same-document include consumes the retained XPath object by calling `xmlXIncludeCopyXPointer` before clearing `incTab[nr]->xptr`.
Traversing the retained XPath node set dereferences freed node memory and triggers the saved heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.note: Source. The current `<xi:include>` node's attacker-controlled XPointer string is read from the XML input and materialized as `fragment`.
The include-table entry retains that XPointer string so same-document load processing later evaluates this exact fragment.
The stored fragment is evaluated against the current document, producing an XPath object whose node set points into `ctxt->doc`.

Root cause. For same-document includes (`doc == NULL` in the vulnerable code), libxml2 stores the evaluated XPath object in the include table instead of copying it immediately, preserving a deferred alias to current-document nodes.
Phase 3 explicitly treats a deferred XPath object as sufficient to revisit an include record, so processing continues later with the stored `xptr` still live.

The same phase-3 replacement logic frees an include node. The saved ASan free stack identifies this site as the prior free for the later UAF read, but static source alone does not prove which deferred `xptr` entry aliases that exact node.
A later same-document include record consumes the retained XPath object during phase 3, calling the copy routine before freeing and clearing `incTab[nr]->xptr`.

Sink. Traversing the retained XPath node set dereferences a node pointer from `obj->nodesetval`; the saved ASan trace proves this read hits freed 120-byte node memory after the earlier `xmlFreeNode(cur)` in the same phase.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The fix removes deferred same-document `xptr` storage rather than changing allocation; the allocation stack is consistent with document nodes later freed before the stale XPath traversal.

format.name: libxml2-xml-xinclude
format.contract: An XML document accepted by libxml2 far enough to invoke `xmlXIncludeProcessFlags`, containing same-document XInclude references whose `xpointer` attributes are exactly the local-fragment trigger mechanism used by the saved witness. This GT only claims the witnessed local-XPointer same-document path, not a broader class of arbitrary XInclude inputs.
